name: ND at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: North Dakota's strong Republican lean (R+18 PVI)
Incumbent Julie Fedorchak seeking reelection with a large financial edge
Prediction markets price Fedorchak near certain to win
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Fedorchak's incumbency, and her roughly nine-to-one fundraising advantage over Trygve Hammer leave no evidence pointing toward an upset, and markets agree at about 96% for Republicans. The forecast stays close to fundamentals with a slight widening for the money gap.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic outside spending or a polling surprise showing Hammer within single digits would warrant a re-rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Dakota's at-large House seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of about 18 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Julie Fedorchak won the seat in 2024 and is running for reelection with the advantages of incumbency in a favorable environment.

Democrat Trygve Hammer faces steep odds: he has raised about $190,000 to Fedorchak's $1.7 million and enters the race with little cash on hand. No public polls track the race, and prediction markets give Fedorchak roughly a 96% chance of winning. Barring an unexpected shift in the political environment, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands comfortably.
